The stellar initial mass function of @Kroupa2001 is a broken power law:

$$
\frac{dN}{dM_\star} \propto M_\star^{-\alpha}, \qquad
\alpha = \begin{cases}
0.3 & M_\star < 0.08\,M_\odot \\
1.3 & 0.08\,M_\odot \le M_\star < 0.5\,M_\odot \\
2.3 & M_\star \ge 0.5\,M_\odot
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-kroupa}

@fig-imf plots @eq-kroupa per logarithmic mass interval.

::: {#cell-fig-imf .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"}
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

m = np.logspace(-2, 2, 400)
dNdm = np.where(m < 0.08, (m / 0.08) ** -0.3,
       np.where(m < 0.5, (m / 0.08) ** -1.3,
                (0.5 / 0.08) ** -1.3 * (m / 0.5) ** -2.3))
dNdlogm = m * dNdm

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.5))
ax.loglog(m, dNdlogm / dNdlogm.max(), color="k")
ax.set(xlabel=r"$M_\star\,(M_\odot)$", ylabel=r"$dN/d\log M_\star$ (normalized)")
plt.show()
```
